correctness.rationale: A fixed point has constant barycentric coordinates on each vertex orbit, so its orbit masses give the inverse to the affine barycenter map from the orbit complex. The relevant model is the independence complex of the admissible-orbit graph, not the induced complex on fixed vertices. The top clique rejects every nontrivial cycle orbit; below the top each such orbit sees all neighboring-level orbit vertices, including its own cycle one level away, because a distinct-label cross pair exists. A fixed-label orbit at the same level has a subset of that neighborhood. For nonadjacent u,v with N(u) contained in N(v), every independent face containing v can adjoin u; remove the pairs F,F∪{u} for F containing v but not u in decreasing cardinality, so each is a free-face collapse. This deletes all nonsingleton orbit vertices when f≥1. When f=0, same-level orbit vertices are twins and the same collapse leaves the apex and one vertex at each level below the top, giving P_(ℓ+1). For P_m, removing its second vertex leaves a cone and that vertex's link is Ind(P_(m−3)); the deletion cofibration yields the suspension recurrence for m≥4 with base cases point, S⁰, S⁰. For f=1 and ℓ≥2 the smaller graph has isolated vertices. For f≥2 the wedge dimensions and multiplicities are exactly Carnero Bravo's Corollary 7 after substituting f, with no depth shift in that convention. The 2019 formulation uses the shifted index ℓ+1.
